docs.title: pixi-policy
docs.text:
Write down what your pixi environments are allowed to contain, and check it everywhere pixi runs. One file, pixi-policy.toml, committed beside pixi.toml and pixi.lock; one command, pixi policy, that reports every package, source, license or manifest setting the policy does not allow, with the reason and a fix hint, and exits non-zero so CI can stop the merge.

pixi policy init     # write a policy the workspace passes today
pixi policy          # check it (the same as `pixi policy check`)
pixi policy explain  # every rule; `pixi policy explain <RULE>` for one, with its keys

pixi-policy reads three files and needs no server and no database. It uses the network only for a shared policy extended by URL, known vulnerabilities and freshness, and caches all three, so a check runs offline once they are cached; a policy with none of them never uses it. It is a single binary that pixi runs as pixi policy.

docs.title: What it checks
docs.text:
Family Rules Checks that Sources sources.channels, sources.indexes, sources.git, sources.url, sources.path conda packages come only from allowed channels, PyPI packages only from allowed indexes, and nothing from git, a direct URL or a local path unless allowed Bans bans.deny no banned package, version range or build is in any environment Licenses licenses.deny, licenses.review, licenses.not-allowed, licenses.unknown, licenses.ambiguous every package can be used under the licenses the policy allows Advisories advisories.vulnerable, advisories.unknown, advisories.unavailable no package has a known vulnerability at or above the policy's severity, known exploited or likely to be exploited Freshness freshness.build-age, freshness.majors-behind, freshness.archived, freshness.unknown, freshness.unavailable no conda package is too old a build, too many major versions behind its channel's newest, or from an archived conda-forge feedstock Hygiene hygiene.conda-pypi-duplicate, hygiene.unavailable no PyPI package is one a conda package in the same environment already provides Python python.older, python.newer, python.requires-python every environment runs the policy's standard Python minor version (any patch release of it), and the pyproject's requires-python starts there Manifest manifest.wildcard-spec, manifest.python-pinned, manifest.required-platforms, manifest.exclude-newer pixi.toml gives no * specs, pins Python to a minor version, lists the required platforms and keeps new releases out for a cooldown (exclude-newer) Lock lock.present, lock.complete, lock.in-sync pixi.lock exists, locks every environment for every platform, and still satisfies the manifest Waivers waivers.expired, waivers.unused, waivers.too-long every exception has a reason and an end date, and still matches something

Every environment and every platform in pixi.lock is checked. The rule catalog says what each rule checks, and the policy file reference lists every key with its type, allowed values and default.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
How Command From PyPI (the wheel carries only the binary) uv tool install pixi-policy, pipx install pixi-policy or pip install pixi-policy In a pixi workspace, pinned with the rest of its tools [feature.lint.pypi-dependencies] pixi-policy = ">=0.1,<0.2" in a feature that has Python, then pixi run -e lint pixi-policy A release archive download it from GitHub Releases and check where it came from with gh attestation verify <archive> --repo aesir-oss/pixi-policy

pixi finds any pixi-<name> executable on PATH, so once pixi-policy is installed pixi policy works. A conda-forge package, for pixi global install, is planned (#6).

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Nothing failed. Warnings may still be reported 1 At least one finding is an error 2 The policy, the manifest or the lockfile could not be read, or the policy loosens a base it extends
